title: Uniform Gaussian approximation for regular thresholds
statement: There is a constant $C>0$ such that the following holds. For every dimension $n$, every $\rho\in(-1,1)$, every $\varepsilon\in\mathbb R$, every coefficient vector $a\in\mathbb R^n$ with $\sum_i a_i^2=1$ and $|a_i|\le\varepsilon$ for every $i$, and every pair of signs $s,t$, the absolute difference between the probability that the correlated random sign vectors’ weighted sum lies in the quadrant determined by $s,t$ and the corresponding centered Gaussian probability with covariance matrix $\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\\rho&1\end{pmatrix}$ is at most $C\varepsilon/\sqrt{1-\rho^2}$.
hypotheses_covered: There exists a positive real constant $C$.
